title: Select the Maximum Number of Affordable Investments
real_world_story: An investor wants to diversify a portfolio across as many investment opportunities as possible. Each opportunity requires a different amount of capital, and the investor has a fixed capital limit.

real_world_connection.target_represents: Maximum number of investment opportunities that can be selected
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Selecting the least expensive opportunities first to maximize the number of selected investments

problem_statement: Given N investment opportunities and their capital requirements, determine the maximum number of opportunities that can be selected without exceeding the available capital. Each opportunity can be selected at most once.
task: Select as many investment opportunities as possible while keeping the total required capital within the available capital.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and C, representing the number of investments and the available capital. The second line contains N space-separated integers representing the capital required for each investment.
output_format: Print the maximum number of investment opportunities that can be selected.

examples.explanation: Selecting investments requiring 2, 3, and 5 units uses 10 units of capital. Four investments would require at least 17 units, exceeding the available capital.
The two least expensive investments require 3 and 4 units, so two investments can be selected within the capital limit.

expected_algorithm.name: Greedy
expected_algorithm.reason: Selecting the least expensive investment opportunities first maximizes the number of opportunities that can fit within the available capital.

hint: Sort the capital requirements in ascending order.
Start with the least expensive investment.
Keep selecting investments while the total capital remains within the limit.
The number of selected investments is the answer.
real_world_takeaway: A greedy strategy can help investors maximize portfolio diversification when the goal is to select the largest possible number of opportunities under a capital constraint.
